note: Every image this repository can build from its own builders, as data. src/Build-Sign-Deploy-UniversalGPU.ps1 executes this catalogue, docs/BUILD_SIGN_DEPLOY.md is rendered from it, and tests/test_image_variants.py checks every builder, switch, output name and attestation against the source. Signing proves authenticity only: nothing here says an image is safe, bootable, or verified on hardware.

selection.label_rule: src/Gpu-Selection-Build.ps1: each SSSS:BB:DD.F with ':' and '.' replaced by '-', joined by '--' for two targets, or N<count>-<12 hex> above two

signing.transport: WSL (wsl.exe) with a base64-encoded bash payload; Windows paths are decoded inside WSL and never cross the command line as path arguments
verifies: the WSL cert's DER form is byte-identical to the Windows .cer you enrolled in the BIOS
the WSL key matches the WSL cert
the unsigned image did not change before, during or after signing
sbverify accepts the signed image with that cert
the signed image is a different file from the unsigned one
signing.db_enrollment: Get-SecureBootUEFI -Name db (X509 EFI_SIGNATURE_LIST scan) proves the signature is the one the firmware already trusts; -SkipDbCheck records db_enrolled=UNKNOWN instead

read-only.why: the diagnostic reads the PCI tree and BAR0-free descriptors; it never writes a GPU register, resets a Falcon, calls a vendor Stop or loads firmware

refuses-before-mutation.why: the preparation build links the active source and refuses before GuInit; it logs BEFORE_MUTATION=1 and returns

compile-only.why: a synthetic-profile image returns before any firmware or GPU operation; it exists to prove the sources compile

stop-only.why: calls the original vendor Stop and may hang; unlock, flash and reset stay disabled

actuates.why: performs an explicitly waived hardware mutation, such as a driver Stop/release or the separate firmware-unlock transaction; the class alone does not imply that an unlock transaction is present or verified

variants.title: Bootable dynamic Stop/release-only test with ASPM admission waiver
variants.note: Bootable EFI application. At each boot it enumerates current PCI devices and selects every currently detected supported NVIDIA GPU in firmware enumeration order, without a compiled BDF list or persistent GuTargets write. Waives ASPM admission. Console policy is topology-dependent: before Stop, the image makes a best-effort attempt to display the warning through configured ConOut, including when the target is the only GOP; this attempt is not a console admission requirement. If that target is the only GOP, release diagnostics use the authoritative file log, then after ConnectController and reattachment graph verification the image makes a best-effort completion display through current ConOut; console-output failure does not invalidate the verified sequence. Otherwise ConOut, ErrOut and the live TextOut graph must resolve to a verified non-target survivor GOP, including an unselected NVIDIA peer. It runs msi_release.c Stop/release, ConnectController reattachment and protocol/GOP graph checks for the live selection, then returns to firmware without launching another EFI program. The pre-Stop warning lists each selected device's live BDF, PCI ID and subsystem ID; successful or unavailable console display is recorded in the file log. vendor/unlock_610.c is excluded and no firmware unlock transaction is called. Displays on listed GPUs may go dark, disconnect or flicker; physical display routing, reattachment, recovery and hardware behavior are unverified. No firmware asset files are loaded and PROM/signature checks are not run. File logging and the live device warning are retained; routine screen output is suppressed. For a fixed ordered subset instead, pass -SelectionBdfs with one or more BDFs when building this stop-only variant; the build embeds and reports that exact order.

variants.title: Dynamic Stop/release-only test with Windows handover after success
variants.note: Uses the same runtime GPU selection, Stop/release and verified reattachment sequence as the Stop-only application. After each verified reattachment, the application makes a best-effort attempt to replace the warning on its original peer display with a success message and target address. After all targets complete, loads the Windows Boot Manager from exactly one detected non-USB EFI system partition. Rechecks the complete GPU sequence, closes the USB log, then starts Windows without a reset. A failed check blocks explicit handover. No fixed BDFs, firmware unlock, flash or NVRAM writes. Windows boot and physical recovery remain unverified.

variants.title: Dynamic DXE Stop/release-only test with ASPM admission waiver
variants.note: Dynamic DXE test that selects all currently detected supported NVIDIA GPUs in firmware enumeration order, without compiled BDFs or persistent GuTargets writes. Waives ASPM admission. Console policy is topology-dependent: before Stop, the image makes a best-effort attempt to display the warning through configured ConOut, including when the target is the only GOP; this attempt is not a console admission requirement. If that target is the only GOP, release diagnostics use the authoritative file log, then after ConnectController and reattachment graph verification the image makes a best-effort completion display through current ConOut; console-output failure does not invalidate the verified sequence. Otherwise ConOut, ErrOut and the live TextOut graph must resolve to a verified non-target survivor GOP, including an unselected NVIDIA peer. Each selected GPU runs msi_release.c driver Stop/release, then ConnectController reattachment and protocol/GOP graph verification. The pre-Stop warning lists each selected device's live BDF, PCI ID and subsystem ID; successful or unavailable console display is recorded in the file log. The vendor gpu_unlock_610 firmware transaction is excluded from the image; UNLOCK=0, FLASH=0, RESET=0. Displays on selected GPUs may go dark, disconnect, or flicker; physical reattachment, recovery and hardware behavior are unverified. No firmware asset files are loaded and PROM/signature checks are not run. File logging and the live device warning are retained; routine screen output is suppressed. The DXE driver returns to firmware after the release sequence. For a fixed ordered subset instead, pass -SelectionBdfs with one or more BDFs when building this stop-only variant; the build embeds and reports that exact order.

not_buildable.why: the unselected mutating Experimental image is deliberately disabled: its mutation path is not generally hardware-safe, and the builder throws if asked
the dual Stop requires a pinned Windows handoff, so a no-handoff dual image has no legal build
a DXE boot-service driver is PE subsystem 11; firmware will not run it as BOOTX64.EFI, and the script refuses to stage one
GU_ESP_RESIDENT gates the launch of an application image; a Driver#### entry is not launched from a volume, so the combination would advertise a gate that cannot run

a preparation-only image cannot also read its targets at boot: src/port.h requires the ordered selected-target mode (GU_ACTIVE_SINGLE_TARGET) for GU_RUNTIME_SELECTION, and src/gpu_discovery.c refuses that mode with a preflight-only profile, so no define set satisfies both - the source needs a preparation profile for runtime target selection first

a preparation-only image cannot also read its targets at boot: src/port.h requires the ordered selected-target mode (GU_ACTIVE_SINGLE_TARGET) for GU_RUNTIME_SELECTION, and src/gpu_discovery.c refuses that mode with a preflight-only profile, so no define set satisfies both - the source needs a preparation profile for runtime target selection first
